card.name: Words introducing a clinical condition
card.fires_on: Words like seen, states, conditions or significance that come right before a clinical condition or setting is named, as in 'may be seen in' or 'clinical states in which'.

modes.label: 'seen' after may be/are
modes.description: The word seen after 'may be' or 'are', introducing the setting where a finding occurs.
modes.example: Bradycardia may be<< seen>> early in phenylephrine overdos

modes.label: states/conditions
modes.description: The nouns states or conditions that introduce a disease setting.
modes.example: in clinical<< states>> in which there exists edema with sodium

modes.label: 'clinical' + noun
modes.description: The noun after 'clinical', as in clinical significance.
modes.example: The clinical<< significance>> of this property is unknown.

card.plain: It fires on small words that lead into a named medical condition or setting, like 'may be seen in' or 'clinical states in which'.
